safe_wording: In the United States almost every newborn gets a hearing screen. Guidelines say it should happen before the baby leaves the hospital, and no later than one month old. In 2020, state programmes recorded a screen for about 98 out of every 100 babies born.

allowed_numbers.how_to_say_it: about 98 out of every 100 babies born in 2020 were screened

'about 98% of babies have their hearing screened before 1 month of age'

confirmed_sources.what_it_confirms: EHDI goal 1: 'All infants should undergo hearing screening prior to discharge from the birth hospital and no later than one month of age'

notes: 98.2% screened (CDC) and 'about 98%' (NIDCD) agree. NIDCD's 'before 1 month' overstates CDC's own data: about 95% of all births were screened by 1 month. So do not attach 'before one month' to 98%. 'Normally before leaving hospital' is a guideline, not a measured rate; phrase it as the guideline. US-only figures; the UK also screens newborns, but nothing UK-specific was checked.

safe_wording: One common newborn test is called an otoacoustic emission test, or OAE. A soft probe in the ear canal plays sounds and listens for a faint sound coming back out of the ear, something like an echo. A healthy inner ear produces it.

'A small earphone, or probe, is placed in your ear'; the probe 'measures the sounds that come back'; 'sounds given off by the inner ear when responding to a sound'; used in newborn screening

notes: Keep 'echo' as an analogy ('something like an echo'): the sound is generated by the cochlea, not reflected off the eardrum. StatPearls' line naming TEOAE/DPOAE as the most common newborn techniques could not be re-opened (Bookshelf blocked); not needed for this wording. Do not claim the test is painless or done asleep (NIDCD says only that babies usually sleep during the tests; leave it out).

safe_wording: That returning sound is made by the outer hair cells of the cochlea, and it has to travel back out through the middle ear. So a clear response is a sign that the outer hair cells, and the middle ear, are working.

confirmed_sources.publisher: Joint Committee on Infant Hearing 2019 position statement
confirmed_sources.what_it_confirms: 'OAE measures a physiologic response from the cochlear outer hair cells'; 'Otoacoustic emissions provide important information about the integrity of the outer hair cells of the cochlea'

confirmed_sources.what_it_confirms: OHCs amplify the travelling wave; 'This also generates a byproduct: a lower-amplitude wave that travels back along the membrane, through the middle ear, and emerges from the external ear canal as an OAE'

safe_wording: An OAE test checks the ear, not the hearing nerve. allowed_numbers.how_to_say_it: about 99.9 percent of the energy would bounce off

confirmed_sources.what_it_confirms: 'almost all (more than 99.9%) of the acoustical energy is reflected'

safe_wording: In 1978 David Kemp, a physicist working at a London ear hospital, played clicks into people's ears and recorded what came back. These sounds are called otoacoustic emissions.
